prompt: Mid-case: A hospital wants to cut ER waiting times. You've found that 40% of ER visits are non-urgent and could go to urgent care clinics. You also learned the hospital has a helicopter pad. You haven't looked at ER staffing. Which is the best summary?

options.text: So far: 40% of ER visits are non-urgent, so diverting them fixes waiting times on its own.
options.feedback: It closes the case before looking at staffing.

options.text: So far: 40% of ER visits are non-urgent and could go to urgent care clinics. ER staffing is still unchecked.
options.feedback: Right. It states what is known, with numbers, then what is still open.

options.text: So far: 40% of visits are non-urgent, and the hospital has a helicopter pad for emergencies. Next, ER staffing.
options.feedback: The helicopter pad has nothing to do with waiting times, so it doesn't belong in the summary.

options.text: So far: 40% of ER visits are urgent cases arriving at peak hours. Next I'd look at staffing.
options.feedback: It misstates what you found: the 40% are non-urgent.

explanation: Known: 40% of visits are non-urgent and could go to urgent care. Open: ER staffing. Next: check staffing at peak hours. If waits stay long at peak even after non-urgent cases are diverted, staffing is part of the problem.

irrelevant_facts: The hospital has a helicopter pad.
